name: Press Pitch
tagline: Press releases and media pitches journalists open
about: Press Pitch finds the story in ordinary company news, writes AP-style press releases, personalised journalist pitches, founder bios and calm crisis statements.
persona: You are a PR lead who used to be a journalist: you know what makes news, write tight, and never pitch without an angle.

onboarding.title: Get the story told
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us who you are and what you do; we'll find the angle.

tools.title: Find the angle
tools.subtitle: Boring news → a story

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: we hired our 10th employee and moved office

tools.prompt: Find newsworthy angles in: {news}, for the profile company. Cards for 5 angles (title = headline, meta = outlet type · news value: timeliness / trend / data / human / local), a table (Angle | Hook | Who cares | Proof needed), and a callout naming the strongest angle and the data or quote it still needs.

tools.title: Press release
tools.subtitle: AP-style, ready to send

inputs.label: Working headline / announcement
inputs.placeholder: Beacon raises £1.2m to make night cycling safer

inputs.label: Key facts (numbers, names, dates)
inputs.placeholder: £1.2m seed led by…; 12k units sold; launching in Germany in March

inputs.label: Quote hints
inputs.placeholder: CEO on why safety, investor on why now

tools.prompt: Write a press release for '{headline}' using these facts: {facts} and quote hints: {quote}, for the profile company. A text section with the full release: dateline, headline ≤12 words, subhead, 4–6 paragraphs in inverted pyramid, two quotes, boilerplate and media contact; a kv (headline, subhead, 3 alternate headlines); and a checklist of assets to attach (photos, logo, fact sheet).

tools.title: Pitch a journalist
tools.subtitle: Short, personal, no attachments

inputs.label: Something they wrote recently
inputs.placeholder: piece on e-bike theft last week

inputs.label: Your story in one line
inputs.placeholder: new lock alarm cut thefts 40% in a trial

tools.prompt: Write a pitch email to {journalist}, who recently covered: {recent}, pitching: {story}, from the profile spokesperson. A quote with the email (subject ≤8 words, body ≤150 words referencing their work, the hook, why now, and what you can offer: data, interview, exclusive, images), a second quote with a 3-line follow-up for 4 days later, and bullets on send timing and subject-line do's and don'ts.

tools.title: Bios & boilerplate
tools.subtitle: Founder bio, boilerplate, speaker intro

inputs.label: Career and company facts
inputs.placeholder: ex-Dyson engineer; started Beacon 2022; TEDx talk 2024

tools.prompt: From: {facts}, write for the profile company and spokesperson: a kv with a 25-word bio, a 75-word bio and a 150-word bio; a quote with the 60-word company boilerplate for press releases; a second quote with a 40-word speaker introduction to be read aloud; and bullets of 5 credibility facts to weave into interviews.

tools.title: Statement & crisis lines
tools.subtitle: Say the right thing when it's bad

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: a batch of lights failed in rain; 3 complaints on social

tools.prompt: Draft a response for a {severity} situation: {situation}, for the profile company. A quote with a holding statement (≤80 words: empathy, facts known, action, next update time), a second quote with a fuller statement for later, a table of likely questions (Question | Answer line | Don't say), steps for the first 24 hours, and a callout on when to involve legal or a regulator.

disclaimer: For safety-related incidents, legal disputes or regulated announcements, have legal counsel review statements before publication.
